method: sha256 over the file bytes and the byte size; no line, row or field was read or counted; the paths derive from v2 SEALED_SCORES_PINNED_BEFORE_THE_READ by replacing SEALED_scores_<DAY>.json with SEALED_feed_<DAY>.jsonl, the same derivation be_race_reader uses
pinned_before: any read of the feed; declaration v3 opens the FEED and pinned no feed digest (0 sixty-four-hex strings in v3, checked)
pinned_by: BE (pm-be), at the close of the day and from the run that produced the feed -- be88fwd06, the `be_forward_day` service unit for 20260906

produced_by.why_it_is_named: v6 rules that the pinned feed's producer is `be_forward_day`; this pin names the run that wrote these bytes so the claim is checkable rather than asserted.

scores_untouched: the five SEALED_scores stay sealed; their v2 digests are not re-verified here

supersedes.rule: 13 / R-608 -- vN+1 by the {path, sha256} PAIR; v1 is NOT edited
supersedes.what_changes: ONE added day in `per_day` (20260906), plus `protocol`, `as_of_utc`, `pinned_by` and two blocks that say which read each day belongs to. Every one of v1's five pins is byte-identical.

the_first_reads_days: 20260901..20260905 are inherited from v1 BYTE-IDENTICAL and belong to the FIRST read, which is opened and closed. `all_five_present` below is v1's own field about those five days and is not a statement about the second read's four.

the_second_reads_days.the_remaining_three: 20260907, 20260908 and 20260909 are pinned at their own closes, each by the next version of this family through the same compare-and-swap -- v3, v4, v5. A landed version is immutable, so `written day by day` is vN+1 three more times, never an edit.
the_second_reads_days.what_this_does_NOT_mean: the whole-set precondition is one quarter met and nothing more. The read refuses until EVERY declared day carries a pin with a digest in this family's chain head; a partial set is not a partial read, and no day is opened by this file.
